reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text:
I love this app in almost every way. The owners are incredibly responsive to App Store reviews, feedback, and any issues that come up. The level of detail throughout the app is amazing.

One of my favorite things is that you can genuinely use it without paying. And even if you do upgrade, there’s a one-time purchase option, which is incredibly refreshing compared to apps that lock everything behind another monthly subscription.

My only major suggestion: please, please gamify the platform more. As someone with severe ADHD who struggles with staying focused and consistent, I think a deeper points/rewards system could be a game changer. The existing energy system is a great start, but I’d love to see things like XP, levels, streaks, achievements, rewards, and even point penalties for missed goals.

Adding that extra layer of progression and dopamine would make self-improvement feel more like a game, something you actually want to keep coming back to every day. For someone like me, that could take an already great app to another level.

reviews.title: A Home Screen Mainstay
reviews.text:
I downloaded Structured a few years ago to see if it could help me manage my ADHD, and honestly wasn’t sure how much I’d actually use it. There are less than 10 apps that have changed my Home Screen layout, and this became one about 3 weeks after downloading it and hasn’t moved since. 

The Inbox is probably what made it click for me. I can just throw everything I need to remember in there (as it comes to me, not at once). Then, if I’m planning my day, I can actually give everything a place and dedicate time to focus on it, or just add things in as I go and set a time limit. It’s helped a ton with both forgetting things and having a million things I know I need to do but no idea where to start. Not to mention the focus timer screen and widgets! 

I was unsure about premium at first, but after using the app for a while I ended up going for it and it’s been worth it every day. The newer Structured AI feature has been especially great. My days obviously never go exactly according to plan, so being able to easily readjust everything when something takes longer or shorter than expected makes the difference of giving up vs calibrating my updated times.

Huge thanks to the people who build and maintain this app. It’s genuinely one of the few productivity apps that has stuck with me for years and actually made my life easier. Also, thank you for putting so much emphasis and effort into making it visually appealing because I definitely cannot focus on a productivity app if I hate looking at it 😂

reviews.title: This app has a great widget! Missing some features in premium
reviews.text:
Overall, Structured is a convenient and beautiful app for quickly seeing what tasks I have ahead of me from my home screen via the widget, and has reliable notifications, and for those reasons, I will continue to use it.

Structured absolutely needs a search function. The premium version needs a way to prevent tons of duplicates from stacking on top of each other. Some pop-up asking if you meant to create a duplicate if the task already exists on a day would be nice. The AI in the premium version isn't very helpful. 

Structured has a checklist with a nice widget and some fun icons to make seeing the tasks easier at a glance.

It has some disadvantages that other apps, such as FlowSavvy, don't have. Some of those disadvantages are: Structured has no search function at all (not even in the premium version), overlapping tasks creating a visual mess (FlowSavvy stacks them next to each other if they overlap, instead of directly above/below as Structured does), and no repeating tasks unless you have premium (FlowSavvy lets you repeat tasks on the free version). 

The search function for Structured has been on their roadmap for almost 4 years. The allowance for overlapping tasks that don't disturb the task flow has been on the roadmap for almost 3 years and was rejected, with no clear reason given.

That said, Structured is quite reasonably priced and even has a lifetime purchase option.

Overall, the app is great! This has to be the best app I’ve ever used.]

I love how the app helps you measure time for each task and throughout the day. I’ve always struggled with measuring time throughout my day and with this app, it has an actual time tracker so you can see how much time you have left before starting your next task. My only suggestion is an alarm sound at the end of each task. There are times I’m in the zone and didn’t realize I spilled over but an alarm sound would be lovely. 

What I also love about the app is how easy it is to swap my tasks around. Other apps, I have to delete the task and retype it on a different day. There are times I over plan my day and have to move the task back or on to different day and with this app, it’s super simple.

I have it synced with my Google Calendar, so I enter all my other tasks for the week directly into the calendar, then drag and drop them around my appointment windows, fitting each task into whatever day and timeslot works. It’s an excellent visual for me, and the app even sends reminders when a task or appointment window is about to start. When I actually listen to those reminders and prioritize them, I arrive on time to work and appointments. I also subscribe to their alarm app, Awake, which is genuinely useful for waking me up at the time I actually set, and making it far less likely that I accidentally sleep in.

reviews.title: I LOVE This App, but the Inbox Is HORRIBLY PAINFUL! Please end the suffering!
reviews.text:
I absolutely love this app except for one thing: The Inbox.

If it wasn’t for the inbox, I would give this app five stars. In fact, I would give it more if I could.

The Inbox is so painful to use on a tablet and especially on a phone if you have a lot of items sitting there that you haven’t scheduled yet. And isn’t that the whole point of an inbox? I put things there because I know I need to do them, I don’t want to forget them, but I don’t necessarily know yet when I’m going to do them.

I currently have around 20 things in my Inbox, and trying to organize them is incredibly frustrating. You have to press and hold each task and drag it where you want it. But if you’re trying to move something farther up the list, once you reach the top of the screen, IT DOESN’T KEEP SCROLLING. It just stops. So you have to let go of the task, scroll the list to make more room at the top, find the task again, drag it farther up, and keep repeating this process.

Why???

There’s also no way to filter or sort the Inbox by category, which would at least make managing a larger Inbox easier.

What frustrates me so much is that I genuinely LOVE this app. I have a lot of plates spinning in my life, with both big and little things I need to remember, and Structured is exactly the kind of app I need. But I’m starting to wonder if the Inbox is actually helping me manage all of those things or just giving me another frustrating list that I have to manage.

Please fix this user experience. At the very least, tasks should continuously scroll when you drag them to the top or bottom of the screen. Even better, give us ways to sort, filter, group, or otherwise organize the Inbox.

I design software, so I understand that development takes time and priorities have to be made. But this feels like such a fundamental usability issue in a core part of the app. Please make it a priority.

I really don’t want to stop using Structured because I love almost everything else about it. But the Inbox is making me want to.

reviews.title: very good app
reviews.text:
this is a very good app -
i am impressed. i downloaded like 6 different planning apps to audit before beginning university and i deleted all but this one. it’s super well rounded and easy to follow but thorough at the same time. the daily planning feature itself is very nice - easy to plan block to block and the blocks get gradually colored / filled as the time goes on in real time so you can see visually how much you have left to do x task. i absolutely love the concept of the energy monitor because one of my biggest traits is over planning and quickly becoming overwhelmed. i think that feature will be very helpful in balancing my university schedule. it also has a section for random thoughts/tasks that come to mind that you can jot down in a list to come back to later in the day. you can also add subtasks to each event you add to your schedule so if i schedule a two hour block for assignments i can add my exact assignments as subtasks and see if i get only 3/4 checked off for example in my time block then i can add the remaining in the “inbox” section for stuff to revisit / reschedule for later. all in all this is a really cool and balanced app (can’t reiterate enough how much i love the energy monitor feature) and when i begin university next month i 1000% intend to purchase lifetime so i can use it through pursuit of my J.D. :)
